summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease, and a history of kidney transplant was admitted for hyperglycemia and neutropenia. He presented with a blood glucose of over 400 and a white blood cell count of 1.7, with ANC of 1040. He reported drinking peach nectar the day before and had slightly decreased appetite. Initial evaluation showed stable cardiomegaly on chest X-ray, no acute infection, and normal renal function. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and CMV viral load was undetectable. The neutropenia was attributed to valganciclovir and ertapenem, both of which were discontinued. His white count improved to 2.0 by discharge. He remained on micafungin for ongoing antifungal treatment. His insulin regimen was continued without change, with plans for outpatient adjustment. An ultrasound showed stable cirrhosis without ascites or biliary obstruction. He was discharged home with home health support for IV therapy and follow-up with transplant and infectious disease clinics.
